who: Historian of American diplomacy and foreign policy at the University of Alabama, retired in 2015.

evidence.says: Alabama's department identifies Jones as its longtime Distinguished Research Professor and a specialist in American diplomatic history.
The Howard Jones scholarship honors the department's longtime diplomatic historian, who retired in 2015.
The candidate's LC record cites The Course of American Diplomacy (1984), identifying its author Howard Jones with the University of Alabama.
The alternative H. S. Jones record identifies a lecturer in French history at the University of Manchester.

notes: Alabama affiliation, period and diplomatic-history field match the students. The Manchester candidate is a different historian.

who: Edward L. Farmer, historian of Ming China at the University of Minnesota; Harvard PhD in history and Far Eastern languages, 1968.

evidence.says: Farmer reports teaching at Minnesota from 1968 to 2010, a Harvard doctorate in 1968, and research interests including Ming China.
The Edward L. Farmer author catalogue lists Early Ming Government and his editorship of Minnesota Studies in Early Modern History.
LC identifies Edward L. Farmer as the author of Technology Transfer and Cultural Subversion (1983).
The catalogue identifies that work as Edward L. Farmer's lecture on the early Jesuit mission to China, published by Minnesota's James Ford Bell Library.

notes: The candidate's name, Chinese-history works and Minnesota connection agree; the Harvard doctorate matches own_phd.

who: Jeffrey R. Collins, historian of early modern political thought formerly at Queen's University.

evidence.says: Queen's History identifies faculty member Jeffrey Collins as Jeffrey R. Collins, author of In the Shadow of Leviathan (2020).
The Jeffrey R. Collins authority cites The Allegiance of Thomas Hobbes and In the Shadow of Leviathan; the latter identifies Queen's University, Ontario.
The department reports Collins's move to Florida and continued doctoral supervision at Queen's.
The alternative candidate's authority identifies Jeffrey G. Collins, author of The Egyptian Elite under Cromer, 1882-1907.

notes: The Queen's affiliation and Hobbes scholarship match the supervision context. The alternative authority concerns Jeffrey G. Collins.

who: Kinley J. Brauer, historian of American diplomacy at Minnesota, 1965-2001; Berkeley history PhD, 1963.

who: Kathi Kern, historian of women and nineteenth-century America at Kentucky; PhD in American history, University of Pennsylvania.

Cornell University Press identifies Kathi Kern as the author of Mrs. Stanton's Bible.
